title: You said you love God.
paragraphs:
You said you love God.
But there’s something you refuse to let go of.
You defend it.
You revisit it.
You make room for it when no one is watching.
And deep down, you’ve asked it—quietly, almost nervously—
Can both stay?
Can I hold onto this… and still hold onto Him?
You already felt the tension the moment that thought crossed your mind.
Because love doesn’t share like that.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior.
There’s a reason your heart tightens when conviction hits. There’s a reason certain sermons make you uncomfortable. Not because God is trying to shame you—but because He’s exposing a divided love.
Jesus didn’t soften this.
“If you love Me, keep My commandments.” (John 14:15)
Read that again.
He didn’t say, “If you love Me, feel something.”
He didn’t say, “If you love Me, say the right words in prayer.”
He tied love to obedience.
Not perfection.
But direction.
Because love moves.
And sin… pulls the opposite way.
You can’t walk north and south at the same time.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
The issue isn’t that you still struggle with sin. Every believer faces that battle. The issue is when sin stops being a battle—and becomes something you protect.
That shift is quiet.
It happens when conviction fades.
When excuses grow louder than Scripture.
When you stop calling it sin and start calling it “just how I am.”
God saw it.
You knew.
And something in you chose not to fight anymore.
That’s where the danger begins.
“Do not love the world or the things in the world. If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him.” (1 John 2:15)
Not weakened.
Not struggling.
Not in him.
That’s not casual language. That’s a line in the sand.
Because love is exclusive at its core.
You can’t deeply love what nailed Christ to the cross—and claim to love the One who was nailed there.
Feel the weight of that.
Jesus didn’t die so you could manage sin. He died to break its power.
“Those who belong to Christ Jesus have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires.” (Galatians 5:24)
Crucified.
Not hidden.
Not justified.
Not kept on life support.
Killed.
And yet, you’ve been feeding something Christ called you to crucify.
You return to it.
You make peace with it.
You even plan around it.
And still say, “I love God.”
This is where everything either collapses… or becomes real.
Because love for God isn’t measured by your words in worship—it’s revealed by what you refuse in secret.
When no one is there.
When it would be easy.
When it would feel good.
That’s where your love speaks the loudest.
“Whoever says ‘I know Him’ but does not keep His commandments is a liar, and the truth is not in him.” (1 John 2:4)
That’s not meant to crush you.
It’s meant to wake you up.
Because there is still grace—but not for pretending.
There is mercy—but not for clinging.
There is forgiveness—but it flows through repentance.
Not around it.
Repentance isn’t just feeling bad. It’s turning. It’s choosing God over the thing you once chose instead of Him.
And yes—it costs something.
It costs the version of you that made peace with sin.
It costs the comfort of doing what you want.
It costs the lie that you can have both.
But what you gain…
You gain freedom.
You gain clarity.
You gain a real relationship with God—not one built on excuses.
You stop living divided.
You stop hiding.
You stop calling darkness “just part of the journey.”
And something changes in you.
Not instantly perfect—but honestly transformed.
Because now, when sin shows up—it’s not something you protect anymore.
It’s something you fight.
That’s the difference.
That’s the evidence.
That’s love.
So no—you cannot love sin and truly love God at the same time.
But you can come out of that place.
Right now.
Not tomorrow.
Not when you “feel ready.”
Now.
You already know what needs to go.
God already put His finger on it.
And this moment—this exact moment—is where the decision happens.
You either keep protecting it…
Or you finally surrender it.
Say it plainly, even if it costs your pride.
Confess it. Bring it into the light. Stop negotiating with something that’s been quietly destroying your intimacy with God.
Let it confront you.
Let it change something.
Not for show—but as a line drawn.
You’ve seen it. You’ve felt it.
Don’t let them drift without truth.
And if you’re ready to go deeper—to be sharpened, corrected, and built in truth consistently—step into it here:

Because the version of you that tries to love both…
won’t survive what God is about to do in your life.
